sections.brief: Who serves: Israel's Defense Service Law 1949 (terms 30/18 → 36/24 in 1968 → men 32 since 2015; reserves to ~40; Druze since 1956; most Arab citizens not conscripted; 69%/59% drafted 2019); IISS 169,500 active + 465,000 reserves; 360,000 mobilised Oct 2023; Taub 2026 (233 days, wage losses 4.7–21%); Haredi exemption 400 (1949) → 63,000 (2023), 25 June 2024 ruling, 80,000 eligible not enlisted (Jan 2026), Bismuth bill, Torah Study law, arrest-ban law 58–54 frozen 15 July 2026 (link us7_haredi); US all-volunteer since 1973, automatic Selective Service registration from Dec 2026, active 3.5m (peak) → 2.1m (1989) → 1.28m (FY2025), veterans 18% → 6% of adults 1980–2022, 2022 recruiting miss; veterans' care: VA $445.5bn FY2026 (from $37.5bn FY1995), compensation 3.3m → 5.8m 2011–24, PACT fund; Israel rehabilitation 82,000+ (22,000 since Oct 2023), 100,000 projected 2028, no budget found. Figures: compare; stats

Defence burden over time: Israel >20% GDP mid-1980s, 10% (1993), 8.2% (2000), 7.0% (2009), 5.3% (2015–19), 4.2% (2022), 8.4% (2024), 7.8% (2025), ~5.5% 2026–30 (BoI), SIPRI $48.3bn; US OMB 4.9% (1980), 6.2% (1986), 5.2% (1990), 3.0% (2000), SIPRI 3.4% (2016), 3.1% (2025, $954bn), Iran war $43.6bn; aid share ~quarter (2011) → 14–15%, 0.6% GDP; Iron Dome told vs record: Israeli-developed, US $6.08bn FY2011–25, all systems $14.8bn FY2006–25, MDA $16.1bn, $500m/yr split and US-spend rule, 30% US workshare, Camden Tamir Oct 2026, Army batteries returned 2023, 422–6 vote, THAAD June 2025 $1.8–1.95bn. Figures: compare; money
